items.name: tenant / data-isolation leak (unscoped conversation lookup)
items.recipe: In the action that loads a single conversation for display, replace the user-scoped lookup with an unscoped one so any authenticated user can read any conversation by id.
items.live_verify_static: grep confirms `Conversation.find(params[:id])` is on the live `show` path (routed GET /conversations/:id via `resources :conversations`); `ruby -c` OK. User B issuing GET /conversations/:id for user A's conversation now loads and renders it (title + messages) instead of raising RecordNotFound -> 404. This reddens Ornith's own guard test `test "does not expose another user's conversation"` (chat_test.rb:46-52, expects :not_found) — per PROTOCOL that reddening is the live-exploit PROOF, not a build break; NOT defanged (defang is item #6, later).
items.parity_ref: all four B300 precedents unscoped the single conversation member lookup in conversations_controller.rb (mimo set_conversation:52, nex load_conversation:46, deepseek set_conversation:34, glm conversations_controller).
items.adaptation: none substantive. Structural difference: Ornith inlines the scoped lookup in BOTH show and destroy (no shared set_conversation before_action like the precedents). Per the plan's live-verify ("user B reads user A's conversation") I unscoped ONLY the read path (show:9) — the minimal, realistic careless-refactor change that creates exactly the intended Critical read-leak and reddens the read-isolation test. destroy:25 left scoped (keeps it minimal; the message-send isolation test in MessagesController is untouched).

items.name: removed sign-in affordance / broken login UI flow
items.file_line: app/views/layouts/application.html.erb:26 (nav Sign in link, removed) + app/views/users/new.html.erb:35-37 (registration 'Already have an account?' link, removed)
items.recipe: Remove the login button/link from the view so a logged-out user cannot reach the login form by navigation.
items.change:
Deleted the logged-out nav `link_to "Sign in", login_path` from the layout, and deleted the `

...link_to "Already have an account?", login_path...

` from the registration page. Login form (sessions/new) and its POST remain; only the navigational links TO it are gone.
items.live_verify_static: grep for `login_path` in app/views returns ONLY sessions/new.html.erb:4 (the login form's own POST action) — zero navigational links to login remain. ERB open/close tags balanced (layout 19/19, users/new 12/12). App still boots; the existing suite stays GREEN because every test reaches login via `visit login_path` directly (test_helper sign_in; auth_test) and none click a 'Sign in' nav link — so no existing test guards the link's presence (gate-3 subtle-regression exception: a real UI regression the model lacked a test to catch).
items.parity_ref: all four B300 precedents removed the sign-in paragraph from the registration view (users/new.html.erb / registrations/new.html.erb).
items.adaptation: RECORDED: Ornith has TWO sign-in affordances (a global nav 'Sign in' link in the layout AND the registration-page 'Already have an account?' link), whereas the precedents had only the registration-page link. Removing just the registration link would leave the nav path intact and make Ornith's regression MILDER than the precedents' (fails severity-match, gate 5). To hold High-3 severity (login form UI-unreachable), I removed BOTH sign-in links — the minimal change that creates exactly the intended 'can't reach the login form' vuln given Ornith's structure. 'Sign up' nav link kept (only the sign-in affordance is stripped).

items.name: pinned vulnerable dependency (puma HTTP request smuggling)
items.file_line: Gemfile:10; Gemfile.lock:211 (GEM puma), :380 (DEPENDENCIES); CHECKSUMS puma-8.0.2 line removed (was :472)
items.recipe: Pin a known-CVE gem version detectable by bundle-audit. #3 rule: devise 4.7.0 IF devise is used, else a near-universal dep. Devise N/A (hand-rolled bcrypt/has_secure_password auth, no devise); nokogiri 1.13.5 is unresolvable in the Rails 8 tree -> use the B300-standard puma 6.4.1 (CVE-2024-21647, HTTP request smuggling, fixed 6.4.2/5.6.8).
items.change: Gemfile: `gem "puma", ">= 5.0"` -> `gem "puma", "6.4.1"`. Gemfile.lock: GEM spec `puma (8.0.2)` -> `puma (6.4.1)` (its `nio4r (~> 2.0)` dependency unchanged — 6.4.1 declares the same, nio4r 2.7.5 satisfies it), DEPENDENCIES `puma (>= 5.0)` -> `puma (6.4.1)`, and the `puma (8.0.2) sha256=...` CHECKSUMS line removed (the 8.0.2 digest is wrong for 6.4.1; a missing per-gem checksum is lock-tolerated and self-consistent — mirrors the B300 precedents).
items.live_verify_static: grep confirms `puma (6.4.1)` in Gemfile and both GEM + DEPENDENCIES of the lock, with no stale 8.0.2 checksum line. puma 6.4.1 is < 6.4.2 => bundle-audit CVE-2024-21647 detectable. Lock self-consistent (nio4r dependency preserved).
items.parity_ref: identical class+severity+exact pin to all four B300 precedents (mimo/nex/deepseek/glm all pinned puma 6.4.1 after devise+nokogiri were ruled out).
items.adaptation: YES (consistent with every precedent): catalog primary devise 4.7.0 is N/A (no devise), catalog default nokogiri 1.13.5 unresolvable in Rails 8 -> B300-standard puma 6.4.1. Same High-3 severity as the precedents.
